items.headline: Nasdaq and S&P 500 bounce Friday, but the Dow slips after Thursday's rout
items.note: On Friday the Nasdaq rose 1.09% to 24,579.42 and the S&P 500 gained 0.32% to 7,376.86, while the Dow fell 0.46% to 51,285.73. Chip stocks led the rebound, but it recovered only a small part of Thursday's drop, when the Nasdaq fell 5.52%. Those closing figures come from a single outlet, so treat them as approximate.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO is likely mid-November on the Nasdaq, at a lower valuation than hoped
items.note: Investors reportedly see $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion, down from the $2 trillion floated earlier. The amended prospectus lists about $895.4 billion of compute and infrastructure commitments, and local data-center ballot measures were opposed in 40 of 41 cases. No offering price has been reported.

items.headline: OpenAI's CFO says data-center spending continues despite voter pushback
items.note: Sarah Friar said the election results didn't change much and OpenAI will keep investing to meet customer demand. She also said a 2027 public debut is still under consideration. For you, it suggests AI infrastructure hiring isn't stopping.

items.headline: October CPI is due Tuesday morning
items.note: Early FactSet estimates are for 3.9% year-over-year inflation, up from 3.7%, with core inflation expected to cool month over month. Friday's strong payrolls report already has investors focused on what the Fed does next. Producer prices follow Friday.

items.headline: Nvidia lost about $440 billion in value Thursday
items.note: The Magnificent Seven together lost about $1 trillion that day as AI stocks led the selling. Nvidia reports later this month, and some strategists are 'nibbling' on beaten-down chip names while others expect more selling.

items.headline: Microsoft is reportedly consolidating its 'neocloud' AI capacity partners
items.note: CNBC reports it plans to lean on fewer suppliers and its own data centers. A slower outside buildout could mean fewer openings at AI infrastructure firms. I didn't re-read the full story today.

items.headline: Meta strategy chief Dave Wehner leaves to be CFO of AI startup Fireworks
items.note: Wehner was Meta's CFO from 2014 to 2022. Fireworks, an AI inference platform, was valued at $17.5 billion in July and is reportedly in early talks to raise at $30 billion to $40 billion.

items.headline: Friday's payrolls report came in strong
items.note: CNBC says the strong report kept attention on Fed policy. That's good for the job market overall, but it can make rate cuts less likely, which weighs on tech stocks. I didn't see the headline job count.

items.headline: Nasdaq entered a correction Thursday; the VIX was around 24 Friday
items.note: CNBC says the S&P 500 is roughly back to where it was in July, after record highs above 7,800 last month. Worries include data-center limits after the Democratic sweep of Congress and a possible year-end shutdown.

items.headline: Take-Two reports earnings today
items.note: It's on CNBC's Monday calendar along with Occidental and KKR. Worth watching if you follow game-industry business.

learn.explain: Headline inflation counts everything consumers buy. Core inflation leaves out food and energy, because those prices jump around with weather, wars and oil. Economists and the Fed watch core to see the underlying trend. Tomorrow's October CPI is expected to show headline inflation rising to 3.9% while core cools month over month. That would mean the increase is coming mostly from volatile prices like energy.
learn.try: When the CPI report comes out Tuesday, compare the headline number with the core number.
